tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the wiki's linked MapBench 0.5.6 summary (bourgesl.github.io/marlin-0.5.6/longer_shared/perf_summary.htm, read from the bourgesl/bourgesl.github.io repo source) compares Marlin 0.5.6 against Oracle JDK 8 Ductus and OpenJDK 8 Pisces and states the CPU (Intel i7 4800 at a fixed 2 GHz, no HT, no turbo), the JDK builds and the full JVM and renderer flags; the harness is public (github.com/bourgesl/mapbench: bin/bench_marlin.sh, bin/bench_pisces.sh, src/, maps/). The wiki's own Marlin 0.3 tables alone would be C (only '4 virtual CPUs', no CPU model).

corrections.claimed_speedup: MapBench 0.5.6 summary (longer shared profile, 9 maps at 1, 2 and 4 threads, ratio = baseline time / Marlin time): overall score versus Ductus 228.90% and versus Pisces 223.85%; per-test ratios versus Ductus range from 99.75% to 598.66%. Summary Pct95 ms/op at 1/2/4 threads: Ductus 157.616 / 263.145 / 645.566, Pisces 345.619 / 373.08 / 477.03, Marlin 0.5.6 129.718 / 130.557 / 131.877, i.e. about 1.22x / 2.02x / 4.90x faster than Ductus and 2.66x / 2.86x / 3.62x faster than Pisces (derived from page data). Wiki Benchmarks page, Marlin 0.3 tables (same ratio direction, checked against the linked compareResults page: Pisces 173.103 ms vs Marlin 102.149 ms gives 169.46%): versus OpenJDK 8 Pisces 'score small' Tavg 163.28% (1 thread), 162.93% (2), 164.92% (4), 'score big' 327.59%, 372.77%, 391.64%; versus JDK 8 Ductus 'score small' 96.28%, 134.03%, 186.95%, 'score big' 128.67%, 164.76%, 386.80%. Wiki headline: 'Marlin 0.5.4 is 17% to 25% faster than marlin 0.3 and is as fast as Oracle ductus !'
corrections.compiler_and_flags: 0.5.6 summary: Oracle Java SE 1.8.0_60-ea-b05 (HotSpot 25.60-b05), plus an internal OpenJDK 1.9.0 build of 2015-02-24 for the extra 'Marlin JDK9' column; JVM tuning -server -Xms2048m -Xmx2048m -XX:+UseConcMarkSweepGC; Pisces via -Xbootclasspath/a:../lib/openjdk8-pisces.jar -Dsun.java2d.renderer=sun.java2d.pisces.PiscesRenderingEngine; Marlin via -Xbootclasspath/p:../lib/marlin-0.5.6-Unsafe-sun-java2d.jar -Xbootclasspath/a:../lib/marlin-0.5.6-Unsafe.jar -Dsun.java2d.renderer.useThreadLocal=true -Dsun.java2d.renderer.useSimplifier=false -Dsun.java2d.renderer.useRef=soft -Dsun.java2d.renderer.pixelsize=2048 -Dsun.java2d.renderer.tileSize_log2=5 -Dsun.java2d.renderer=org.marlin.pisces.PiscesRenderingEngine; MapBench 0.4. Wiki 0.3 tables: custom OpenJDK8 b65 build (Pisces and Marlin), JDK8 b121 (Ductus), heap 2g, minimum 5000 ms per test.
corrections.hardware: 0.5.6 summary: Intel i7 4800 (as written on the page; host HP ZBook 15), 4 CPUs at a fixed 2 GHz, HyperThreading and turbo boost disabled, Linux 3.13.0-47 (Ubuntu). Wiki 0.3 tables: 4 virtual CPUs on Linux 2.6.35 (Fedora 14), CPU model not stated.
corrections.workload: MapBench 0.4 (Java 2D rendering of serialized GeoServer map drawings, maps/ in the mapbench repo) at 1, 2 and 4 threads: longer shared profile (one image per test, 10 s per test; 27 tests, 9 per thread count) for the 0.5.6 summary; default and shared profiles for the wiki's 0.3 and 0.5.4 comparisons.
corrections.caveats: Java, not C++: a pure-Java Java 2D RenderingEngine plugged into the JDK through sun.java2d.renderer, derived from the OpenJDK 8 Pisces source (GPL-2.0 with Classpath exception). Pisces (OpenJDK 6-8) and Ductus (closed-source, Sun/Oracle JDK up to 8) were the default Java 2D antialiasing rasterizers before Marlin replaced them in OpenJDK 9 (JEP 265, per the README's JDK table), so they are recognisable incumbents for Java but not catalogue baselines (Skia, Cairo, Blend2D): baseline_in_list false. All numbers are first-party and from 2014-2015 builds (Marlin 0.3 to 0.5.6; current release 0.9.4.9) on early-access or internal JDK builds; since Marlin is now the JDK default, the comparison is historical and Ductus is only available as a binary in Oracle JDK 8. Summary ratios are Pct95 per-op times under concurrent threads, so the 4-thread gain over Ductus largely reflects Ductus's poor multi-thread scaling; single-thread gain over Ductus is about 1.2x (0.5.6) or none (0.3 'score small' 96.28%). The result pages live on bourgesl.github.io (blocked here; read from the bourgesl/bourgesl.github.io repository source); the wiki's newer charts (0.7.x, FOSDEM 2016) are images that were not read.

notes: Wiki numbers match the record exactly; the 0.3 detail page names no CPU model, but the linked 0.5.6 summary does (Intel i7 4800, fixed 2 GHz), so the tier rises to A. Metadata checked on github.com: GPL2 + Classpath exception, 197 stars, not a fork, last master commit 2025-10-06 (README update; release 0.9.4.9 Oct 2025), active. Language stays Java and baseline_in_list stays false.

tier_reason: README 'Sample Benchmark' shows the four ops/s figures from the project's own benny script (benchmark/bench.ts) with no machine, Node version or build settings; first-party with partial methodology, so C.

corrections.baseline: sharp (libvips, which renders SVG through librsvg and Cairo), svg2img (canvg plus node-canvas, which is Cairo-based) and skr-canvas (@napi-rs/canvas, Skia-based)
corrections.claimed_speedup: README 'resize width' suite: resvg-js (Rust) 12 ops/s, sharp 9 ops/s, skr-canvas (Rust) 7 ops/s, svg2img (canvg and node-canvas) 6 ops/s. About 1.3x sharp, 1.7x skr-canvas and 2x svg2img (derived from page data).
corrections.workload: README 'Sample Benchmark', 'resize width' suite run with benny: render example/text.svg (1324x687, 79 paths, linear gradients, one text element) to PNG at a width of 1200 px with a background colour. benchmark/bench.ts also has 'resize icon width' and 'default options and no text' (tiger.svg) suites whose results are not published.
corrections.caveats: resvg-js is a Node.js (napi-rs) and WebAssembly wrapper around the Rust resvg crate, which rasterizes through tiny-skia (catalogued at A in this wave); resvg itself is not catalogued because it publishes no numbers, so under the wrapper rule this may fold into tiny-skia as a duplicate. The benchmark measures a whole SVG-to-PNG pipeline (parse, render, PNG encode) through Node packages, not a rasterizer: the Cairo and Skia underneath the baselines sit behind librsvg, canvg and Skia's SVG loader, so baseline_in_list stays false. The README result is one integer ops/s per library with no hardware, Node version or package versions, and it predates the current script (the skr-canvas case is commented out in benchmark/bench.ts, last changed 2023-02-07; benchmarks date from 2021-2022). Small fairness issues in bench.ts: sharp reads the SVG from disk each iteration while resvg-js gets an in-memory buffer; resvg-js runs with loadSystemFonts false and no font files, so its one text element is likely skipped while librsvg draws it; svg2img's callback is not awaited, so benny may time only its synchronous part.

notes: Plainly a Node.js/WASM binding of resvg (Rust), not a rasterizer of its own; orchestrator may record decision duplicate (of linebender/tiny-skia) or keep as the only measured resvg entry. Comparison is against sharp, svg2img/node-canvas and skr-canvas, not Inkscape. Metadata checked: MPL-2.0, about 2.0k stars, 80 forks, not a fork, last commit 2026-03-26, active; language is Rust core with a TypeScript/JavaScript Node API.

tier_reason: README comparison table comes from the public bench/compare_test.go, but the CPU is only 'cloud Xeon @ 2.1 GHz' and the Go toolchain for the run is not stated; first-party, and the 477x hatch ratio (>50x, from a bounding-box-bound use of the baseline) caps it at C anyway.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Go; the comparison lives in the separate bench module (bench/go.mod: go 1.26.0, golang.org/x/image v0.46.0, github.com/gogpu/gg v0.52.5; the core module's go.mod says go 1.24); exact toolchain version for the table not stated; run with `cd bench && go test -bench .` (bench/compare_test.go).
corrections.workload: Synthetic print-style scenes on an A3 landscape page at 150 dpi (2481x1754 px) from internal/scenes: Hatch (2,000 parallel 45-degree hairlines spanning the page, drawn one device pixel wide) and Short (20,000 random 2-8 mm strokes, 0.35 mm wide). stilus draws through its Canvas with a page clip; the x/image/vector run strokes each line with stilus's own stroker and fills each outline with one vector.Rasterizer reset to that outline's bounding box; gogpu/gg strokes each line with no clip.
corrections.caveats: The 477x hatch ratio is not a fair measure of x/image/vector: that rasterizer is a dense area accumulator whose cost is proportional to the canvas it is sized to, and the harness resets and draws one rasterizer per 45-degree page-spanning line, so each of 2,000 lines pays for a bounding box of up to about 1754x1754 px; a single page-sized rasterizer filled with all outlines (same result for opaque black) would very likely narrow the gap by orders of magnitude, but that was not measured. The short-stroke row (about 2.0x, derived from page data: 111 ms vs 55 ms) is the representative comparison, and it includes stilus's own stroker on both sides. x/image/vector is the Go project's glyph-oriented rasterizer and gogpu/gg a community library, neither a catalogue baseline (Skia, Cairo, Blend2D), so baseline_in_list is false; quality is only checked against PDFium (mean deviation 0.3-1.5/255, SSIM at least 0.998). The comparison's stilus hatch time (70 ms) does not match the Numbers table's hairline hatch (53 ms), so the tables were likely measured at different times. First-party, one author, repo created days ago (0 stars), CPU model not named exactly, benchmark source read but not run.

notes: Numbers on README match the record (33,400 ms / 70 ms is 477x, 111 / 55 is 2.0x, derived from page data). Comparison is unfair on hatch lines (per-line bounding-box rasterizers for page-spanning diagonals) and roughly fair on short strokes.
